property_summary: For every admissible input the reference contract's transfer(...) call that completes (does not revert) returns true; the mutant returns false for the same completing calls, so there exists an input where the returned boolean differs (bug breaks this rule).

For every admissible call to transfer that succeeds (does not revert), the reference C returns true; the mutant returns false for some successful calls, so asserting that transfer(...) returns true distinguishes them.

For any inputs where transfer(...) completes (does not revert), the reference C returns true; the one-instruction mutant returns false for some completing inputs, so asserting that a successful call yields true distinguishes them.

For any caller and valid non-empty _tos/v arrays where caller is the hardcoded owner, C.transfer(...) always returns true (completes and returns true); the mutant flips the returned boolean to false so some admissible inputs will make the return value differ.

For every admissible input where transfer(...) is called by the hardcoded owner with a non-empty _tos array and the callee calls succeed, the reference C returns true; the mutant returns false for at least some such inputs, so the return value should always be true on the reference but can be false on the mutant.
